correctness.rationale: From the source equations one obtains S'= -S/(3AB) and D'= -D/(AB), so dD/dS=3D/S and D/S^3 is constant. Substitution gives AB=S^2(1-c^2S^4)/4 and the separable equation S'=-4/[3S(1-c^2S^4)]. Because |c|S_0^2=|A_0-B_0|/(A_0+B_0)<1 and S decreases, positivity persists until S=0. Exact integration yields the displayed trajectory and extinction time. The anisotropy identity follows from delta=cS^2, and local inversion of the exact remaining-time polynomial gives the stated asymptotics. All new algebra is replayed by the bundled checker.

value.rationale: The S^2 x S^2 product is the primary source's canonical finite-time extinction example and its unnormalized behavior is presented only qualitatively. The first integral completely resolves the product trajectory, gives the exact extinction clock for arbitrary positive initial factor sizes, and quantifies the rate at which the two factors become round relative to each other. This is a natural structural completion of a central explicit example, not an arbitrary parameter slice or routine numerical refinement.
